html:
The Muscogee, or Creek, are a Native American people of the Southeastern Woodlands, from what is now Georgia and Alabama. Their towns were heirs of the Mississippian chiefdoms that Hernando de Soto met in 1540.

After disease and slave raids broke those chiefdoms, the surviving towns joined in a loose confederacy. The English called them Creeks after Ochese Creek in Georgia. The Upper Towns lay on the Coosa and Tallapoosa rivers, the Lower Towns on the Chattahoochee, and towns of other languages, such as Hitchiti, joined them. Through the 1700s the Creek played Britain, France and Spain against each other and were among the strongest nations of the South.

A civil war among the Creek drew in the United States in 1813. Andrew Jackson's victory at the Battle of Horseshoe Bend in 1814 cost them much of their land, and in the 1830s they were forced west on the Trail of Tears. Some who fled to Florida joined the Seminole. See also Mvskoke on the modern map.
